[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#ado-feature-template]

# ADO Feature Template

Use this template when creating or updating Features in Azure DevOps via MCP. Features decompose an Epic into deliverable capabilities — each Feature should be completable within a single Program Increment (PI) or release cycle.
page_texts.3:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#title]

### Title

Short, specific title describing the capability. Do not prefix with "Feature:" — ADO already knows the work item type.

**Format:** `<Verb> <Specific Capability>`

**Examples:**

- Real-time Eligibility Verification via 270/271
- Pharmacy Claim DUR Edit Processing
- Provider NPI Validation and NPPES Sync
- MCO Capitation Rate Cell Configuration
page_texts.4:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#description]

### Description

Structure the description using this format:

```markdown
## Purpose

What this Feature delivers and why it matters to the business.
Reference the parent Epic's goals to show alignment.

## Functional Overview

What the system will do — described from the business perspective, not technical implementation.

Key behaviors:
- <Behavior 1>
- <Behavior 2>
- <Behavior 3>

## Acceptance Criteria

High-level criteria for the Feature as a whole. Detailed Given/When/Then criteria belong on individual User Stories.

- [ ] <Outcome that proves this Feature works>
- [ ] <Outcome that proves this Feature works>

## Business Rules

Domain logic or constraints that apply across all User Stories in this Feature.
Reference `docs/requirements/business-rules/` if documented there.

## Non-Functional Requirements

Quality attributes specific to this Feature:
- **Performance:** <e.g., 270/271 response within 2 seconds>
- **Availability:** <e.g., 99.9% uptime during enrollment periods>
- **Security:** <e.g., PHI encryption at rest and in transit>
- **Compliance:** <e.g., HIPAA, CMS MECT checklist item>

## Dependencies

- Other Features or Epics this depends on
- External systems or integrations required
- Architecture decisions (ADRs) that must be finalized first
```
page_texts.5:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#priority]

### Priority

Map to ADO priority values:

| ADO Priority | Meaning | Maps to BA Priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 - Critical | Regulatory or contractual obligation | P0 |
| 2 - High | Core functionality or major business need | P1 |
| 3 - Medium | Important but not blocking | P2 |
| 4 - Low | Nice to have | P3 |
page_texts.6:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#story-points-feature-level]

### Story Points (Feature-level)

Optional rollup estimate. If used, this is the sum of child User Story points — do not estimate independently.
page_texts.7:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#area-path]

### Area Path

Set to the team or domain area (e.g., `MMES\Claims`, `MMES\Eligibility`). Must match the parent Epic's area or be a child of it.
page_texts.8:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#iteration-path]

### Iteration Path

Set to the target PI or release iteration. Features should be completable within a single PI.
page_texts.9:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#tags]

### Tags

Inherit parent Epic tags and add Feature-specific tags:

- Integration type (e.g., `x12`, `fhir`, `edi`, `rest-api`)
- Domain concern (e.g., `dur`, `prior-auth`, `enrollment`)
- `breaking-change` if this Feature changes existing behavior
page_texts.10:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#links]

### Links

- **Parent Epic** — ADO parent link (required)
- **Child User Stories** — ADO parent/child links
- **Related Requirements** — link to `docs/requirements/functional/` and `docs/requirements/non-functional/` files
- **Architecture Decisions** — link to governing ADRs in `docs/decisions/`
- **Related Features** — ADO related link for cross-Feature dependencies
page_texts.11:
[.claude/templates/ado/feature.md#guidelines]

## Guidelines

- One Feature per deliverable capability — if it takes more than one PI, break it down further
- Features must have a parent Epic — orphan Features indicate a scope gap
- Write acceptance criteria at the business outcome level — technical validation belongs on User Stories
- Include NFRs on the Feature, not buried in individual stories — they apply to the whole capability
- Reference domain terms from `docs/glossary.md` or domain glossaries in `docs/design/conceptual/domains/<domain>/glossary.md`
- When creating a Feature, also create or update the corresponding task entry in `docs/project-plan.md` with the `AB#<id>` reference
- Map to existing requirements in `docs/requirements/` — if no requirement exists, ask the user to invoke `/business-analyst` to create one first
